decision_conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date hereof.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

All external facing materials, treatments and finishes shall be similar to those of the original building and maintained and retained thereafter. This applies unless differences are shown on the drawings we have approved. Reason: To ensure that the extension harmonises with the existing building and to ensure compliance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

No development shall commence until a Construction Method Statement (CMS) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved document shall provide details regarding: - Measures to control dust, dirt, noise, and vibration emissions during site preparation and construction.- Site delivery routes, loading and unloading areas, contractor parking, and material storage.  - Measures to prevent the deposit of mud and debris on the public highway.  The development shall be executed in full accordance with the approved CMS throughout the construction period.  Reason: To safeguard neighbour amenity and maintain highway safety and circulation during construction works, to comply with Policy 29 (Protecting Amenity), Policy 34 (Environmental Protection), and Policy 36 (Transport Impact) of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the first occupation or use of the community hall hereby permitted, a Noise Management Plan (NMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The NMP shall detail operational noise controls, including restrictions on amplified sound, procedures for managing visitor arrivals/departures, and measures to ensure windows and doors remain closed during events. The operational measures approved within the plan shall be permanently adhered to thereafter.  Reason: To ensure the ongoing management of activities within the hall protects neighbouring occupiers from adverse acoustic impacts, to comply with Policy 29 (Protecting Amenity) and Policy 34 (Environmental Protection) of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The community hall hereby permitted shall only operate between the hours of 09:00 and 19:00 on any day, in strict accordance with the operational parameters set out within the Noise Impact Assessment prepared by ES Acoustics.  Reason: To safeguard the living conditions and residential amenities of nearby occupiers from noise and disturbance, to comply with Policy 29 (Protecting Amenity) and Policy 34 (Environmental Protection) of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the installation of any new mechanical plant, extract, or ventilation equipment associated with the development hereby permitted, an acoustic report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall demonstrate that the rating level of noise emitted from all plant will be at least 5 dBA lower than the existing background noise level at any given time of operation, measured at 1 metre externally from any window of the nearest residential facade in accordance with British Standard 4142:2014.  Reason: To prevent noise pollution and safeguard the residential amenity of neighbouring properties, to comply with Policy 29 (Protecting Amenity) and Policy 34 (Environmental Protection) of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the first occupation of the community hall hereby approved, a detailed soft landscaping scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall reflect the submitted Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment (Tunley Environmental, Rev B) and Proposed Layout (Drawing 1771 201), and shall include:  - Details of all proposed soft planting, rain gardens, and new native boundary hedging (including species, planting size, and numbers);- A 5-year maintenance schedule.  All soft landscaping shall be carried out in accordance with the approved scheme in the first planting season following completion of the development. Any trees or plants which within a period of 5 years from the completion of the development die, are removed, or become seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species.  Reason: To secure high-quality soft landscaping, protect visual amenities, and secure the delivery of a minimum 10% Biodiversity Net Gain on-site, to comply with Policy 26 (Biodiversity) and Policy 28 (Character and Design) of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the first occupation of the development, full details of the following highways and parking measures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:  - Type, specification, and secure visual details of the cycle parking facilities.  - Road markings and directional signage to clearly indicate and enforce the internal one-way vehicular traffic layout.  The cycle parking, parking layout, and one-way signage shall be installed prior to first occupation in accordance with the approved details and retained permanently thereafter.  Reason: To encourage sustainable modes of transport, prevent vehicular conflict on-site, and ensure safe access and parking provision, to comply with Policy 36 (Transport Impact) and Policy 37 (Parking) of the Sutton Local Plan 2018, and Policy T5 (Cycling) of the London Plan 2021

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Fire Safety Statement by CGA Design & Build.Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with the Mayor's London Plan Policy D12.
